name: Nearby Wi-Fi devices
plain: Lets the app find and connect to nearby Wi-Fi devices without needing location.
meaning: Reveals nearby access points and peers; the neverForLocation flag declares the app does not derive location. Also the interim grant for Android 16 local network protection.

android.note: Replaces location requirement for Wi-Fi Direct and Aware on Android 13.

ios.prompt_ui: Location prompt plus entitlement; join prompt for NEHotspotConfiguration
ios.note: No Wi-Fi scan API; SSID needs location plus entitlement (iOS 13+).

data.update: scan throttled to 4 per 2 minutes foreground

limits.headline: Can find and connect to nearby Wi-Fi devices without needing your location
limits.user_action: You tap Allow for Nearby devices when the app asks
can: Find nearby devices for Wi-Fi Direct or Wi-Fi Aware on Android 13 and newer
Connect straight to a nearby device
Use Multipeer Connectivity on iPhone to find nearby apps
cannot: Scan for Wi-Fi networks on iPhone; no scan feature exists
See your Wi-Fi name on iPhone without the entitlement and location
Find your location when the app says it never uses location for this
Use it before you allow Nearby devices
limits.differs: Android 13 and newer split this from location. iPhone has no scan and needs entitlements for Wi-Fi names.

story.what_it_is: An app finds and connects to nearby Wi-Fi devices without needing your location.

marketing.name: Nearby Wi-Fi devices
marketing.pitch: Android 13 lets apps find and connect to nearby Wi-Fi devices without location access.

story.for_you: You see a prompt for Nearby devices. If you allow it, the app can find speakers, printers or direct Wi-Fi links. You do not have to give your location.
story.for_makers: Makers get a cleaner permission that does not scare people with a location prompt. They promise not to use it to work out where you are. It also helps with the new local network limits on Android 16.

use_cases.example: A smart plug app finds a new device nearby without asking for location.
A file share app sends photos to a nearby phone directly.
A local multiplayer game links phones with Wi-Fi Direct.
A speaker app finds a new speaker on first setup.
A warehouse app connects to a handheld scanner using Wi-Fi Direct.
An app declares that it will not use the permission to work out location.

story.android_note: Android 13 added this permission, with a flag that says the app does not derive location.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no matching permission, since it uses the local network prompt.

technical_bounds: iOS has no scan API for apps

history.change: Local Network Protection uses NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES as the interim grant
